item.title: TEST KITCHEN: The improbable instant Ramen recipe
item.description: If I say, “Guess where I heard about this recipe,” and you answer, “Wait, wait, don’t tell me,” you would be right. As in the NPR quiz game show.

item.title: Bestselling author Len Deighton dies at 97
item.description: LONDON — Len Deighton, a prolific writer whose tough, stylish spy thrillers featured on bestseller lists for decades, has died. He was 97.

item.title: Eagles set to sign ‘Hollywood’ Brown; Broncos trade for Dolphins’ Waddle
item.description: Wide receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown and the Philadelphia Eagles have agreed on a one-year deal, a person with knowledge of the contract told The Associated Press on Tuesday.

item.title: Howard gets its first March Madness win, holding off UMBC in First Four
item.description: DAYTON, Ohio — Bryce Harris had 19 points and 14 rebounds, and he sank a turnaround jumper with 13 seconds remaining that sent Howard to its first NCAA Tournament victory in program history, 86-83 over UMBC in the First Four on Tuesday night.

item.title: Venezuela overcomes late Harper homer to beat US in WBC final
item.description: MIAMI — Venezuela won the World Baseball Classic for the first time, rebounding from a blown eighth-inning lead to beat the United States 3-2 Tuesday night on Eugenio Suárez’s tiebreaking double in the ninth.

item.title: Sugarloaf Twp. supervisors reorganize following chairman’s death
item.description: The Sugarloaf Township Board of Supervisors reorganized at Tuesday’s meeting following the death of the Chairman Joseph DiSabella.

item.title: PIAA Girls Basketball: Crestwood’s run ends in 5A state semifinals
item.description: BETHLEHEM — Two factors turned Crestwood’s five-point halftime lead Tuesday night into a heartbreaking 45-41 loss to Archbishop Wood in a PIAA Class 5A girls basketball semifinal game.

item.title: Editorial: Where is the transparency in detention center contracts?
item.description: Forget, for the moment, the notion of the Department of Homeland Security literally planning to “warehouse” humans — buy warehouses and convert them into immigration detention centers in various states, including Pennsylvania (as reported in a Spotlight PA story in Tuesday’s paper).

item.title: Op-Ed: No pitcher calls their own strikes; public notices require the same independence
item.description: Life is hectic. Keeping track of work, home, and family commitments is challenging enough. Now imagine adding another task to your daily routine: checking multiple government websites just to find out what your local and state officials are planning to do.
